assumptions_checked.details: The indexing poset has order-preserving shifts P_epsilon for all real epsilon, P_0=id, P_epsilon>=id for epsilon>=0, and P_(epsilon+delta)=P_epsilon P_delta. Thus shifts are invertible. Modules are functors to vector spaces over an arbitrary fixed field; pfd is specified when required. There is no standing finite-barcode assumption.

A refinement replaces each indecomposable barcode summand by a module in that summand's erosion neighborhood and takes their direct sum. It may split a summand but may not combine distinct original summands.

assumptions_checked.locator: Definitions 3.2, 3.8 and 3.10, PDF pp.12,15 / printed pp.950,953
assumptions_checked.details: Im_epsilon(M)=im(M_-epsilon->0), Ker_epsilon(M)=ker(M_0->epsilon). EN_epsilon(M) consists, up to isomorphism, of A/B with B subset A subset M, Im_epsilon(M) subset A and B subset Ker_epsilon(M). Both composites of an epsilon-interleaving equal the relevant 2epsilon shift maps.
For T=M_0->2epsilon, I is largest with f(I) subset T(I) for every f:M->M(2epsilon). K is smallest in I with (T|I)^(-1)(f(K)) subset K for every such f. Pruning is (I/K)(-epsilon).

assumptions_checked.locator: Lemma 5.3 and Theorem 5.4, PDF pp.36,38 / printed pp.974,976
assumptions_checked.details: The source explicitly allows supdim M in {0,1,...,infinity}. The theorem requires M,N pfd and r=supdim M<infinity. Part (i) needs only psi(epsilon) phi=M_0->2epsilon; part (ii) additionally needs the reverse interleaving identity. No r>=1 hypothesis is printed.

reasoning: The first isomorphism theorem identifies Er_epsilon(M)=Im_epsilon(M)/(Im_epsilon(M) intersect Ker_epsilon(M)) with im(M_-epsilon->epsilon). The alternative representatives in Remark 3.3 follow from the second isomorphism theorem.

For pfd modules the subquotient relation is antisymmetric: if A/B is a subquotient of M with all pointwise dimensions equal to those of M, finite dimensionality forces A_p=M_p and B_p=0 at every point. Mutual subquotients therefore give an isomorphism. Transitivity follows by pulling back the intermediate monomorphism along the epimorphism.
Images of the shift morphisms commute with direct sums of vector spaces, so erosion commutes with arbitrary direct sums.
Applying erosion twice yields the image of the composite shift M_(-epsilon-delta)->(epsilon+delta), proving Er_epsilon Er_delta(M) is isomorphic to Er_(epsilon+delta)(M).

Monomorphisms and epimorphisms induce the corresponding maps between the images of the shift morphisms. This verifies the content of Lemma 3.7 without relying on the swapped quotient variable names in one displayed proof line.
boundary_checks: EN_0(M) contains only the isomorphism class of M.
An erosion or refinement of the zero module is zero.

locators: Lemmas 3.9, 3.11-3.12 and Theorem 3.13, PDF pp.15-17 / printed pp.953-955
reasoning: For Q=A/B in EN_epsilon(M), the shift M_0->epsilon induces M->Q(epsilon), since its image lies in A(epsilon), and Q->M(epsilon), since B is killed by the shift. Both composites are induced by M_0->2epsilon and equal the requisite shift maps. This proves Theorem 3.13 exactly, with factor epsilon.

For an epsilon-interleaving N(-epsilon)->M->N(epsilon), the intermediate image quotient im(phi)/(ker(psi) intersect im(phi)) is isomorphic to Er_epsilon(N). The two interleaving equations imply im(phi) contains Im_(2epsilon)(M) and ker(psi) is contained in Ker_(2epsilon)(M), proving Lemma 3.12.

For Lemma 3.11 the auxiliary K=(Ker_epsilon(M) intersect Im_epsilon(M))+B gives the required canonical erosion representative below A/B. The argument uses the embedded submodules, not merely an abstract subquotient comparison.
Direct-sum image and kernel identities put every epsilon-refinement in EN_epsilon(M). This verifies that subsequent interleaving conclusions apply to the particular refinement definition.
These checks do not identify EN_epsilon(M) with all subquotients that happen to be epsilon-interleaved with M; the source correctly distinguishes those notions.

checked_results.scope: Existence in Definition 4.15 for general modules, and the explicit recurrence in the pfd setting used by the main theorem.
reasoning: There is a direct existence proof for the largest I without exchanging a map with a countable intersection: the sum of all submodules J satisfying f(J) subset T(J) for every f has the same property, because linear maps commute with sums. It contains every such J.

For this I, the set of eligible K is nonempty since K=I is eligible. An intersection of eligible K's is eligible: f(intersection K_a) is contained in intersection f(K_a), and preimages preserve intersections. Thus the intersection gives the smallest K.

For pfd M, the source's descending recurrence I_i stabilizes at each point, so the required passage through a descending intersection is valid pointwise. The increasing K_i recurrence commutes with directed unions and is well-defined once I is fixed.

If supdim M=r<infinity, the pointwise recurrences involve fixed linear maps on M_p and can have at most r strict inclusions. Equality at one stage forces equality at every later stage. Hence I=I_r and K=K_r uniformly.
With J_0=M(2epsilon) and J_(i+1)=T(intersection_f f^(-1)(J_i)), induction gives Im_(2i epsilon)(M(2epsilon)) subset J_i. The same dimension bound yields T(I)=J_r, proving Lemma 5.3(i).

For the kernel recurrence, f|I maps I into I(2epsilon) because f(I) subset T(I). Naturality carries Ker_(2(i-1)epsilon)(I) into the corresponding shifted kernel, and taking T-preimages gives K_i subset Ker_(2i epsilon)(I). This proves Lemma 5.3(ii).
Choosing the structural shift among the morphisms gives K=T|I^(-1)(T(K)). Applying T to T|I^(-1)(f(K)) subset K gives f(K) subset T(K); here f(K) subset T(I) is used. These verify parts (iii)-(iv).
checked_results.limitation: The arbitrary-module omega-intersection formula in Lemma 5.2 is not certified; see the explicit limitation below. This limitation does not affect the verified finite-dimensional stabilization used for the main theorem.

locators: Theorem 5.4 and Lemmas 5.7-5.8, PDF pp.38-39 / printed pp.976-977
reasoning: Write N as the direct sum of its indecomposable N_j, and set f_j=psi_j(epsilon) phi_j. The sum of these maps is T=M_0->2epsilon. The pointwise direct-sum structure makes this sum well-defined, including infinite barcode index sets.

Let A_j=psi_j(epsilon)^(-1)(T(I)) and B_j=phi_j(K). The inclusion f_j(I) subset T(I) implies B_j subset A_j. Lemma 5.3(i)-(ii) and naturality imply Im_(2r epsilon)(N_j(epsilon)) subset A_j and B_j subset Ker_(2r epsilon)(N_j(epsilon)). Thus A_j/B_j lies in the required erosion neighborhood.
The maps I/K -> directsum_j(A_j/B_j) -> T(I)/T(K) are well-defined because each f_j preserves I and K in the precise image sense supplied by pruning.

Their composite is the map induced by T. Its kernel is zero by the saturation K=T|I^(-1)(T(K)), and it is surjective by definition of T(I). The splitting lemma therefore makes I/K a direct summand of the constructed refinement of N(epsilon).
Shifting by -epsilon gives exactly Pru_epsilon(M), so the theorem's shift convention and its barcode inclusion agree. Part (i) remains valid when M=0.

checked_results.scope: r>=1, with the local ambient-submodule clarification documented below.
locators: Proof of Theorem 5.4(ii), PDF pp.39-42 / printed pp.977-980
reasoning: The reverse interleaving identity implies psi(epsilon)^(-1)(T(K)) is contained in Ker_(2r epsilon)(N(epsilon)). The calculation uses T(K) killed after 2(r-1)epsilon and therefore requires r>=1. Coordinate projections preserve this structural kernel, giving Z_j subset Ker_(2r epsilon)(N_j(epsilon)).

The proof needs to remove a module isomorphic to the kernel of the induced psi map while respecting the original N_j components. The replacement copies may lie in the corresponding Zbar_j and need not lie in that original kernel.

For a chain of partial decompositions, pfd makes all decompositions locally finite. At a fixed point only finitely many original summands are active, and the decreasing finite-dimensional residual subspaces stabilize. One chain element therefore realizes the proposed limit at that point, verifying the direct-sum conditions for the upper bound.

The local-ring step with an infinite index set can be justified explicitly. Write id_Y=sum_j h_j with h_j=pi_Y pi_j iota_Y. Choose a point p with Y_p nonzero; only finitely many pi_j have nonzero components at p. If every h_j were a nonunit, their finite sum h_F would lie in the maximal ideal of the local endomorphism ring, so 1-h_F would be a unit. But (1-h_F)_p=0, a contradiction. Hence some h_i is a unit.

This unit makes pi_i(Y) an isomorphic direct summand of the residual N_i^S. The new complement preserves the first direct-sum decomposition. Equation (8) supplies spanning for the decomposition with the original processed summands, and pointwise dimension equality makes that sum direct.
The final lifting argument places pi_i(Y) in Zbar_i. It uses that Y and the ORIGINAL processed summands belong to the kernel; it does not use that their replacement copies belong to the kernel.

After all kernel summands are exchanged, Krull-Schmidt cancellation gives a remaining module isomorphic to I/K. Cancellation is legitimate here because every fixed nonzero isomorphism class has finite multiplicity in a pfd module. Each removed coordinate piece lies in Zbar_j, so the enlarged denominator remains inside Ker_(2r epsilon) while the required numerator image is retained. Thus the remainder is a 2r epsilon-refinement.
checked_results.limitations: This supports the intended proof after removing the surplus kernel restriction on replacement copies. It is not a claim that every printed auxiliary condition is maintained as written.

findings.title: The factor 2r requires a positive-dimension qualification when the first module is zero
locators: Definition 3.8 and 3.10, PDF p.15 / printed p.953
Definition of supdim, PDF p.36 / printed p.974
Theorem 5.4(ii), Corollaries 5.5-5.6, PDF p.38 / printed p.976
findings.source_claim: The source explicitly allows r=supdim M=0 and states the 2r epsilon-refinement conclusions with only r<infinity.
findings.counterexample: Take P=R^2 with diagonal shifts, M=0, and N the interval module on [0,1)^2 over any field. Let epsilon=1.
hypothesis_check: The square is an order-convex connected interval. N is nonzero and pfd, with pointwise dimension at most one. M is pfd and r=supdim M=0.

Both interleaving maps can be zero. The composite on M is zero, and N_0->2epsilon is also zero because every point of the square is shifted outside the square. Thus the full epsilon-interleaving hypotheses hold.
findings.contradiction: EN_0(N) consists only of N, since Im_0(N)=N and Ker_0(N)=0. More generally every 0-refinement of a pfd module is isomorphic to that module. Thus 0 is not a 0-refinement of the nonzero N, contradicting Theorem 5.4(ii) and Corollary 5.5.
findings.distance_calculation: For this interval N, N_0->2delta vanishes exactly when 2delta>=1. Hence d_I(0,N)=1/2. A common refinement with 0 must be zero; zero belongs to EN_delta(N) exactly when Im_delta(N) is contained in Ker_delta(N), equivalently N_0->2delta=0. Therefore f_R(0,N)=1/2 as well, while the right side of Corollary 5.6 is 2r d_I(0,N)=0.
findings.repair: State the affected assertions for r>=1, or replace r by max{1,r}.
findings.repair_check: For r>=1 the proof checked above applies. If r=0 and M,N are epsilon-interleaved, then N_0->2epsilon=0, and each indecomposable summand can be replaced by zero within EN_epsilon. Thus zero is already an epsilon-refinement of N, so the max{1,r} version with tolerance 2epsilon holds. For epsilon=0, an interleaving with zero forces N=0.
findings.counterevidence: The zero module is used throughout the source and is not globally excluded; the printed range of supdim explicitly includes zero. The witness is a two-parameter pfd module and does not rely on infinite-dimensional or nonattained-distance subtleties.
findings.impact: A local boundary-domain omission. It does not refute the positive-dimensional stability mechanism or its factor growing with r.

proof_clarifications.disposition: Local proof clarification for the parent to decide whether to report separately or as a coverage note; not promoted to a second counterexample to the theorem.
locators: PDF p.40 / printed p.978, definition of partial decomposition
PDF p.42 / printed p.980, final inclusion in Zbar_i
proof_clarifications.printed_condition: Each replacement X^S is required to be a submodule of ker(bar psi(epsilon)).
proof_clarifications.problem: The exchange sets Y^T=pi_i(Y). A coordinate projection of a kernel summand need not remain in the kernel, and the last paragraph proves only pi_i(Y) subset Zbar_i. For example, a diagonal line in k^2 projects isomorphically to a coordinate line that is not contained in the diagonal line.
exact_replacement_conditions: Take X^S to be a submodule of the ambient Nbar, rather than requiring X^S subset ker(bar psi(epsilon)).
Retain (i) X^S is isomorphic to the original X.
Retain (ii) X^S subset Zbar_j for the component j to which X is assigned.
Retain both direct-sum identities in (iii): Nbar=(directsum_j N_j^S) directsum (directsum_processed X^S)=(directsum_j N_j^S) directsum (directsum_processed ORIGINAL X).
The ORIGINAL X continue to be the summands of ker(bar psi(epsilon)); that property is not changed.
proof_clarifications.repair_verification: The chain upper-bound proof only uses the fixed replacement modules and the two direct-sum identities. The unit/exchange step projects along the decomposition with ORIGINAL processed summands. Equation (8) and the final lifting argument use kernel membership only for Y and those ORIGINAL summands. The replacement copies are used for their coordinate location in Zbar_j, their isomorphism types, and their direct-sum decomposition. Thus no downstream step needs replacement copies to stay in the original kernel, and all stated extension checks go through with the corrected ambient condition.

proof_clarifications.observed_issue: The proof passes from f(I) subset T(I_i) for every i to f(I) subset T(intersection_i I_i), using only that the I_i descend. A linear image does not in general commute with a descending infinite intersection.
proof_clarifications.linear_algebra_counterevidence: Let V have algebraic basis e_0,e_1,..., let V_i=span{e_n:n>=i}, and let T(e_n)=1 in the field. Then intersection_i V_i=0 but intersection_i T(V_i)=k.
proof_clarifications.limitation: This linear-algebra example is not claimed to realize the full all-morphism pruning recurrence. No counterexample to the unrestricted formula itself has been established in this bounded check.
proof_clarifications.verified_scope: For pfd modules each pointwise chain stabilizes, and the passage is valid. The main theorem has the stronger uniform finite bound and is unaffected by this particular limitation. General existence of the largest I and smallest K is independently verified by sums and intersections, as recorded above.

An epsilon-refinement replaces each indecomposable barcode summand by an object in its epsilon erosion neighborhood; it permits splitting but not gluing original summands.
EN_delta(M) means A/B with Im_delta(M) subset A subset M and B subset A intersect Ker_delta(M), up to isomorphism; a subquotient conclusion must not be replaced by arbitrary proximity.

For an upset U, Ker_epsilon(U)=0 and Im_epsilon(U)=U(-epsilon), so every erosion-neighborhood object is an upset V satisfying U(-epsilon) subset V subset U. Nonzero upset modules cannot split into two nonzero upset summands because two upsets share an upper point.
This proves Lemmas 6.3-6.4, including infinite index sets when the direct sums are pfd and barcode uniqueness is used.

checks.topic: Theorem 5.9 sharpness statement and quantitative scope
details: The theorem constructs 1-interleaved M directsum Q and N1 directsum N2, not M alone interleaved with N1 directsum N2.
For each integer n>=2, supdim(M)=2n, supdim(Q)<=2n-1, and for every 0<=delta<n-1 every R in EN_delta(M) has an indecomposable component not a subquotient of either Ni.
The inequality delta<n-1 is strict. The result prevents improvements beyond approximately factors 4 and 8 in the specified parts of Theorem 5.4; it does not establish exact optimality of 2r.
The n=2 boundary is meaningful (0<=delta<1), and the construction and rank arguments use no division by the field characteristic.

checks.assessment_note: Substantive argument verified with the local inclusion correction in finding L0446-F1.
details: At p=(2n^2+7n,2n^2+7n), all 2n coordinate generators are present. For r<=p and 0<=delta<n-1 the source-to-shift maps have no kernel, because r+delta remains below all terminal deletion boundaries. Im_delta(M)_p=M_p.

For q_i'=q_i+(delta,delta), the birth spacing n and delta<n-1 give M_{q_i}=M_{q_i'}=span(e_i,...,e_2n). A direct splitting at p therefore induces complementary flags and a partition of pivot indices beta_V,beta_W.

The x,y,z tests force c~c+n and c~c+n-1 for c<=n-1. These edges connect indices 1,...,2n-1. The c=n test then forces 2n into the same part: span(e_2n) cannot lie in the indicated proper coordinate prefix or in the sum-zero difference subspace.

For c<=n-1, among the bounded difference generators in E only e_c-e_(c+n) touches coordinate c or c+n; the analogous fact holds for F. This justifies the pivot argument over any field, including characteristic 2.

At p, Lemma 5.10 forces any nonzero barcode component of R at p to have dimension 2n: apply it to that component versus the direct sum of the rest. Hence at least one indecomposable has dimension 2n at p.

checks.assessment_note: The necessary rank bound survives the second local correction in finding L0446-F1.
checks.topic: Theorem 5.9 morphism and Lemma 5.12 block interleaving
details: The scalar-map criterion of Lemma 5.11 follows by naturality from the containment of birth upsets and death upsets. The coordinate map f(e_i)=e_(i+1), f(e_2n)=e_2n is well-defined on ambient intervals after the unit shift.

Its restriction to M respects each generator: q_i+(1,1)>=q_(i+1), x_i+(1,1)=x_(i+1), and the y,z difference generators map to the next clamped difference generator or zero. The final e_2n generators remain valid.

Im f has no e1 coordinate. The required bound rank(T-f)<=2n-1 follows because if M_x has dimension below 2n it is immediate, and if M_x=k^(2n), e_2n is a nonzero kernel vector as f(e_2n)=T(e_2n). The printed stronger image-containment statement is unnecessary and fails at a terminal boundary.

Writing T for the natural epsilon transition, the shifted block maps phi=[[f,T],[T-f,-T]] and psi=[[T,T],[T-f,-f]] have both products T^2 times the identity, using naturality f(epsilon)T=T(epsilon)f. The image-factor definitions in Lemma 5.12 ensure the blocks land in the specified submodules.
The Q summand factors through f and so also has pointwise rank at most 2n-1. Together with Lemma 5.10 this proves the required obstruction by pointwise dimension of subquotients.

checks.topic: Constrained-invertibility correspondence and explicit lower bound c<3
details: For finite upset sums, every component morphism is a scalar when the source upset is contained in the shifted target and is zero otherwise. Interleaving compositions are precisely inverse-matrix equations. A simple CI solution is a permutation and its inverse, hence a matching.

Example 6.7 has A=[[1,1,1],[1,0,1],[1,1,0]] and B=[[-1,1,1],[1,-1,0],[1,0,-1]]. Direct multiplication gives AB=I over every field. The two last rows have only column 1 available for a mutually allowed permutation edge, violating Hall for those two rows.

Odd graph path lengths encode inclusions after repeated shifts. Consequently the finite example and Lemma 6.12 give 1-interleaved upset sums with no c-matching for c<3. This supports the stated lower bound, not the open existence of a universal c.

checks.assessment_note: Read floor_odd(c) as the greatest odd integer <=c; the printed word 'smallest' is a local definition typo.
details: For a graph with 2n vertices, finite shortest paths have length at most 2n-1; the unreachable sentinel C+2n exceeds these. Antidiagonal anchors separated by at least C+2n encode the shortest-path coordinate vectors as upset corners.

For 0<=c<=C, componentwise w_i>=z_j-c is equivalent to a directed path u_i to v_j of length <=c. The forward implication uses the coordinate belonging to u_i (distance zero there); the reverse implication is the triangle inequality for path lengths, with the sentinel treating unreachable vertices.

Cross-anchor domination cannot create a false containment: if the own-coordinate inequality fails, that coordinate is below C+2n-c, while domination by a different anchor would require it to be at least C+2n-c.
Bipartite paths from one side to the other have odd length, so weakening uses the largest odd integer <=c. The literal phrase 'smallest odd integer less than or equal to c' should be corrected.
The d>2 product extension adds [0,infinity) factors and preserves the needed nonnegative-shift containments. No interleaving below 1 is possible because every cross-part path has length at least 1.
The U/V scalar-matrix orientation is consistently interpretable after exchanging the inverse matrices where needed; this does not alter existence or the simple-solution correspondence.
The computational input is a finite list of finitely generated upsets (and a finite zero/star CI pattern); the trivial zero and infinite distances are explicitly separated before the theorem.

For the constructed modules and C large enough, distance lies in {1,3,...,c} or is at least c+2. An approximation r in [d,(c+2)d) separates unsolvable original CI (r>=c+2 implies d>1) from a solvable c-weakening (r<c+2 implies d<=c). The open upper endpoint is essential at d=1.

Conversely, finitely generated upset containments yield O(n^2) candidate critical shifts. A positive gap-oracle answer at delta gives d<=c delta, and the least positive candidate satisfies delta<=d because the true critical d cannot receive a valid negative answer. Returning c delta is within the stated factor.

This is an equivalence of computational problems, not an unconditional efficient algorithm for computing the interleaving distance. No complexity hardness citation beyond the paper's internal reduction was independently re-proved.

checks.assessment_note: The printed finite reduction in Theorem 6.14 is terse; the following native argument verifies the extension rather than treating it as a counterexample.
checks.topic: Theorem 6.14 extension from finite CI to pfd upset sums
details: The theorem allows infinite pfd upset barcodes. Pfd alone does not imply a finite barcode: births can escape to infinity. There is no standing finite-barcode hypothesis that may silently be inserted.

Let k be the greatest odd integer <=c. A fixed epsilon-interleaving of pfd upset sums gives mutually inverse column-finite scalar matrices A:X->Y and B:Y->X on algebraic direct sums. Each column has finite support: choose p in its source upset; every nonzero component target contains p+epsilon, and pfd gives only finitely many such targets. Component compositions agree with the scalar equations BA=I and AB=I because upset structure maps are identities on a common upper region.

Form the directed support graph of A and B. Given a finite set S on either side, all vertices reachable from S in at most 2k directed steps form a finite set F, since each outgoing column support is finite. Protect the outgoing columns of A for X0=F intersect X and of B for Y0=F intersect Y.

Set U=span(X0)+B(span(Y0)) and V=A(U)=A(span(X0))+span(Y0). U and V lie in finite coordinate spaces X1,Y1, and A:U->V is an isomorphism. Enlarge/pad the finite coordinate spaces to equal dimension and extend this isomorphism by bases to A'. Its inverse B' agrees with B on span(Y0), while A' agrees with A on span(X0).

The finite zero/star patterns of A',B' form a solvable CI problem. No new outgoing edge starts at a protected vertex. Hence a path of length <=k from S, and any return path of length <=k from its endpoint, are the same as original support paths: their total distance from S is at most 2k. A simple solution of the finite k-weakening therefore injects S into its original mutual-k-path neighbors.

This proves finite Hall inequalities on both sides of the original c epsilon matching graph; actual-support paths imply valid c epsilon containments by Lemma 6.11. This matching graph is locally finite: fixing p in Ui, every matched candidate Vj contains p+c epsilon, so there are finitely many by pfd, and symmetrically on the other side.

Apply the locally finite infinite Hall theorem on each side to obtain injections given by matching edges. The matching version of the Schroeder-Bernstein construction combines them into a bijection using only their allowed edges. All nonzero upset summands must be matched, since no nonzero upset is epsilon-trivial. The epsilon=0 case follows directly from an isomorphism and barcode uniqueness.

Thus the finite CI statement does imply the full pfd matching statement. The omitted finite-locality argument can be supplied without changing the constant. The reverse implication is already the finite construction of Lemma 6.12; Lemma 6.4 gives equivalence with common refinements.
For an order-convex interval I, E(I)=U(I)\I is an upset. The order I<=J means both birth-upset and death-upset containment, and is not the subquotient relation.

Under I<=J, the pointwise identity on U(I)\E(J) is a natural transformation. When I intersect J is an interval, connectedness makes every nonzero component scalar constant throughout the intersection.

Benignness is essential: it supplies the order and connected intersection for nonzero morphisms. If U(I) is not contained in E(K), a point outside E(K) lies in all three supports, so scalar weights multiply under composition. If I<=J(epsilon) and J<=I(epsilon), the canonical scalar maps compose to the shift transitions.

Intervals with a minimum element are benign: a nonzero morphism forces the source minimum into the target, then naturality at death points forces E(I) subset E(J); the common minimum yields intersection connectedness. Upsets are also benign by upward closure and scalar constancy.
These arguments support the claimed classes of hooks, rectangles with finite birth coordinates, and upsets. They do not establish the property for all arbitrary intervals.

checks.assessment_note: The substantive block argument is valid after consistent source/target index labels; several printed labels are typographical.
checks.topic: Theorem 6.18 block completion and unmatched intervals
details: The statement explicitly assumes finite barcodes and a shift-closed benign interval class. This finite condition is retained.

With the usual column-source convention, A is n by m and B is m by n. C=[[A,I_n],[I_m-BA,-B]] maps coordinates (M,N(epsilon)) to (N,M(epsilon)); D=[[B,I_m],[I_n-AB,-A]] maps back. Block multiplication gives CD=I and DC=I without assuming AB=I or BA=I.

The graph columns of C are labeled by M,N(epsilon) and its rows by N,M(epsilon). The paper's prose swaps 'rows' and 'columns' and has associated index labels that require this consistent interpretation.

Every ordinary nonzero block edge X->Y gives X<=Y(epsilon) by benignness; backward identity edges from a shifted copy are immediate. For an exceptional entry (I_m-BA)_(k,i)!=0, if U(I_i) were not contained in E(I_k(2epsilon)), the nonzero composed maps through J_j(epsilon) would all have weight products by Lemma 6.16(iii), and the interleaving identity would force (BA)_(k,i)=delta_(k,i), a contradiction. Therefore exceptional forward edges satisfy U(I_i) subset E(I_k(2epsilon)). The same argument holds on N.

A simple solution of the c-weakening gives a bijection M union N(epsilon) -> N union M(epsilon). Keep matches M->N. If Ii maps to Ik(epsilon), it is unmatched; likewise an unmatched Jj has preimage in N(epsilon), not M(epsilon). These are the appropriate corrected labels.

An unmatched Ii has a path of length r<=c to Ik(epsilon) and a return path of length r'<=c. The outgoing path necessarily crosses an exceptional forward edge from an unshifted to a shifted vertex. Chaining the order inclusions and that death containment gives U(Ii) subset E(Ii((r+r')epsilon)) subset E(Ii(2c epsilon)); hence Ii is c epsilon-trivial. The same reasoning covers unmatched Jj.

Matched M->N pairs have order containment in both directions after c epsilon shifts and hence are c epsilon-interleaved by Lemma 6.16(iv). This proves the conditional matching conclusion. The proof does not resolve the CI conjecture.

checks.topic: Conjectures, practical claims, and code scope
details: Conjectures 6.1, 6.5, 6.10 and the hoped-for pruning-distance result remain conjectural. Section 6 proves equivalences and conditional implications, not their unconditional truth.
The Conclusion treats efficient pruning algorithms and realistic examples as future work. No empirical benchmark or implementation result is presented as already established in these sections.

The source manifest's optional code and supplement statuses are 'not_located_in_bounded_search'. This is inherited acquisition evidence, not a new exhaustive absence claim; no code absence is treated as a mathematical defect.
No author code, numerical simulation, external bibliography or newer source version was executed/inspected in this helper task.

findings.assessment_note: Local corrections to the sharpness proof; the theorem's dimension obstruction is preserved by explicit verified repairs.
findings.title: Two local coordinate assertions in the sharpness proof are stronger than required and false at valid parameter values
findings.location: Lemma 5.10 displayed coordinate-prefix equality on p.982; proof of Theorem 5.9 last paragraph on p.983.
assertions: It then claims that e_(2n) never occurs in the image of T-f, because that image lies in the span of adjacent coordinate differences at every point.
decisive_evidence: Take n=3,c=1,delta=0. Here x_1=(19,13), no q/y/z generator lies below x_1, and only x_1's coordinate generator is born there, so M_{x_1}=span(e1), whereas k^{c+n-2}=span(e1,e2). All stated hypotheses hold.

Take n=2, input point (24,24), and output after unit shift (25,25). All four source coordinates are present; at the output I1 has died while I2,I3,I4 are present. The images under T-f of e1,e2,e3 are -e2,e2-e3,e3-e4. Thus (T-f)(-e1-e2-e3)=e4, contradicting the asserted exclusion and global sum-zero image containment.
counterevidence_and_repair: Since 0<=delta<n-1, floor(delta)<=n-2. The correct inclusion M_{x_c+(delta,delta)} subset k^{c+n-2} supplies exactly the bound used in the pivot proof.

For T-f, if dim M_x<2n, its rank is already <=2n-1. If dim M_x=2n, e_(2n) is a nonzero kernel vector because f(e_(2n))=T(e_(2n)). This proves the needed rank bound at every point, including terminal-boundary points.

The rest of the flag argument, image-factor construction, block interleaving and subquotient dimension obstruction were positively checked. These examples do not refute Theorem 5.9 or its strict lower-bound claim.
findings.impact: Both printed local claims need correction for a literal proof, but the intended result and constants survive the supplied local repairs.
findings.recommended_action: Replace the coordinate equality by inclusion and replace the global image-containment explanation by the pointwise rank/kernel argument.

editorial_notes.note: The definition of floor_odd(c) should say greatest, not smallest, odd integer <=c; otherwise the later c-weakening formulas have no intended literal meaning.
Theorem 6.18 contains source/target and dummy-label typos. The verified consistent block interpretation is recorded in L0446-11. These were not inflated into independent material findings.

limitations: This is a bounded native helper scientific receipt, not the final paper review, compiler audit or independent acceptance.
The main pruning theorem and distance results were assigned to the parent/core helper; no completed sibling or other paper was reviewed here.
The finite-to-pfd argument is new native analytic support, not a claim that the paper explicitly contains that proof.
No empirical program was promised in the checked sections; no missing code defect is inferred.
Source manifests and historical acquisition records remain unchanged; legacy metadata text may contain historical encoding artifacts, while current receipt mathematical strings are ASCII.

checks.claim: The printed d_E fails the triangle inequality.
checks.proof: For half-open interval modules, Er_e(k_[a,b))=k_[a+e,b-e), with the empty interval interpreted as zero. M=k_[0,2) and N=k_[0,1) directsum k_[1,2) have identical pointwise dimensions, including at t=1, hence d_E(M,N)=0. The distance from either to zero is half its longest interval length, so d_E(M,0)=1 and d_E(N,0)=1/2. Thus 1<=0+1/2 is false.
checks.counterevidence: The order in the actual source is pointwise dimension order, not comparison of ranks of all structure maps. All modules are pfd. The paper itself uses this pair to show d_E(M,N)=0. The separate d_EN and its proofs do not use a triangle inequality for d_E.
checks.scope: Local auxiliary-definition defect; no refutation of the cited external erosion distances or of d_EN.
checks.repair: Withdraw the distance designation for this formula, or state an appropriate corrected invariant/order and prove its properties.

checks.proof: For N=I/K in EN_e(M), take inverse images I',K' of a representative J/L in EN_d(N). I' contains Im_d(I), hence Im_(e+d)(M). A d-shift sends K' into K and a subsequent e-shift kills it, proving K' subset Ker_(e+d)(M). For the triangle construction, if Q_i=A_i/B_i are common-neighborhood representatives in N, set A3=A1 intersect A2 and B3=(B1+B2) intersect A3. Under pi1:A1->Q1, Im_d(Q1) is contained in pi1(A3), while pi1(B3) is killed by the d-shift. The latter follows from (B1+Ker_d(N)) intersect A1=B1+Ker_d(A1). Therefore Q3=A3/B3 lies in EN_d(Q1) and EN_e(Q2), and composition gives the claimed triangle inequality. Approximate infima by admissible radii; no attainment assumption is required.

For an e-interleaving phi,psi define M1=Im_e(M)+im psi(-e), M2=M1 intersect Ker_e(M) intersect ker phi and analogously N1,N2. Maps mu,nu from M(-e) directsum N(-e) have respective images M1,N1. Naturality and interleaving imply M_shift mu=psi nu and phi mu=N_shift nu. Thus mu^-1(M2)=nu^-1(N2), yielding an isomorphism M1/M2=N1/N2 in both erosion neighborhoods. Conversely, EN_e and EN_d imply e- and d-interleavings with the common module, whose composition is an (e+d)-interleaving. This verifies d_EN<=d_I<=2d_EN for the stated arbitrary-module scope.

For half-open interval barcodes, a quotient/inclusion pair with e-trivial kernel/cokernel matches every bar of length strictly greater than 2e to a bar [c,d) with a<=c<=a+e and b-e<=d<=b. Composing the two matchings through the common module bounds matched endpoint differences by e; unmatched bars have length at most2e and are e-interleaved with zero. Direct sums give the stated interleaving. Exactly length2e half-open bars may be left unmatched; the proof only needs the strict-longer threshold. The actual source explicitly delegates general endpoint decorations to its cited induced matching result.
checks.limits: No independent reproof of the external matching theorem for all decorated endpoints.

checks.proof: For A_i=[-i,0), B_i=[-i,i), erosion by1 sends B_i to B_(i-1) and A_(2c) to[-2c+1,-1), which embeds as a subquotient of B_(2c-1). A_(2c) cannot be matched with B_i at radius below c since max(i,2c-i)>=c, and cannot be unmatched since its length is2c. For Lemma4.11 the claimed radius1 barcode matching and quotient maps are explicit. Any putative EN_e representative of N for e<c+1 must retain the B_(c+1) generator at -c-1 and its nonzero image at0, while N has zero structure map between those points. Thus the exclusion follows. Obvious sign/inclusion typographical slips are not used as substantive counterexamples.

Given the cited density of finitely presentable indecomposables, choose approximating sequences for M,N. Assumption(ii) makes both distances from each original module to its approximants tend to zero. Both triangle inequalities then identify each distance with the same limit of values on indecomposables, including the extended-value case.
checks.limits: The external indecomposable-density theorem itself was not independently reproved.

checks.proof: Krull-Schmidt uniqueness permits grouping indecomposable summands of each refinement by its parent summand. EN composition and transitivity of subquotients give refinement composition for finite and infinite radii. To prove d_P triangle, apply the first refinement relation at delta=e'+gamma and the second at delta=gamma, then compose infinity-refinements; repeat in reverse direction. Infimum estimates use actual admissible radii.

For a module with pointwise dimension at most1, any submodule splits along its indecomposable summands pointwise, and inherited image/kernel conditions prove EN membership summandwise. In4.22, within each thin summand, the union B_i'' union A_i'' is a submodule because at each point both subspaces are nested (zero or the same one-dimensional space); equivalently it is their sum. The common quotient lies in EN_d(A_i) by the image and kernel inclusions used in4.5, and thinness turns this into a refinement by4.21. Refinement composition yields the triangle inequality. For one-parameter4.23, direct sums of common EN representatives construct a common refinement from a matching; the converse follows from4.9 and algebraic stability. The upset case is delegated to the separate Section6 check.
